title: Level 1 Physics, Earth and Space Science — Energy (2025)
subject: science

questions.text:
A builder uses a 300 Watt electric winch to lift a 25 kilogram bucket of tools to the top of a 15 metre scaffolding from the ground. It takes 15 seconds to lift the bucket from the ground to the top.

Describe the energy changes as the winch lifts the bucket up the side of the scaffolding.
questions.expectedAnswer: Electrical energy is transformed into gravitational potential energy and kinetic energy, with some lost as thermal/heat energy.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: Correct answer identifying that electrical energy is transformed into gravitational potential energy, kinetic energy, and thermal/heat energy.

questions.text:
Compare the amount of energy provided by the winch with the gain in gravitational potential energy of the bucket when it is at the top of the scaffolding.

In your answer, you should:
- consider the amount of electrical energy provided by the winch
- consider the amount of gravitational potential energy gained by the bucket from the ground to a height of 15 m
- explain why there is a difference between these two numbers.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Selected the correct equation for either calculation and put in some numbers.
- Mentions energy loss.

For Merit:
- Both calculations correct.
- Explained the energy loss as heat or sound.

For Excellence:
- Both calculations with correct equation, working, and units.
- Explained where the loss of energy comes from (heat from friction in the motor, sound).

questions.text:
The bucket is at the top of the scaffolding and the cable snaps.

Discuss the energy transfer of the bucket from the top of the scaffolding to when it is halfway down.

You may use diagrams or words (or both) for your answer.
questions.expectedAnswer: Gravitational potential energy is converted to kinetic energy and thermal energy.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Transfer from Ep to Ek + Ep.

For Merit:
- Transfer from Ep to Ek + Ep + Ethermal, showing that at halfway the bucket has lost half its original Ep, gained Ek and some thermal energy from air resistance.

questions.text:
The bucket falls from 15 m.

Discuss the speed of the bucket just before it hits the ground.

In your answer, you will need to:
- calculate the maximum speed at which the bucket hits the ground
- include any assumptions you have made in this calculation
- explain why the bucket will not reach this speed.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Selected correct formula for kinetic energy and added some values.
- Assumed all Ep is transformed into Ek.
- Mentioned energy lost due to friction.

For Merit:
- Correct process with minor error.
- Explains speed will be less due to air resistance / thermal energy / heat.

For Excellence:
- Correct calculation (v = 17.3 m/s) with correct unit.
- Correct assumption (assuming all Ep converts to Ek / no energy loss).
- Energy is lost to thermal due to air particles hitting the bucket surface.
- Therefore the bucket will not hit the ground as fast as the calculated speed.

questions.text:
Mere is in the lounge and wants to warm the room. She switches on a convection heater.

Compare the concepts of temperature and heat energy.
questions.expectedAnswer: Temperature is the average kinetic energy of the particles, whereas thermal/heat energy is the total kinetic energy of all the particles.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Either definition correct.

For Merit:
- Has explained a difference between temperature and thermal/heat energy.

questions.text:
Mere notices the maximum power rating for the heater is 2400 W.

The voltage supply in her house is 230 V.

She sets the dial to 50% maximum.

Calculate the current in the heater circuit.

Include the correct units.
questions.markingGuide:
At 50% maximum, P = 1200 W. I = 1200/230 = 5.22 A (accept 5.2 A).

WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Shows correct equation with some numbers.

For Merit:
- Correct answer with working and units.

questions.text:
Mere turns the dial on the heater, which increases the current in the heater.

Discuss how an increase in current in the circuit affects the amount of thermal energy released by the heater.

Use relevant formulae to support your answer; calculations are not required.
questions.expectedAnswer: Increase in current causes increase in power (P = VI). Increase in power causes increase in energy output (E = Pt).
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Increase in current increases electrical energy.
- OR increase in power causes increase in energy.

For Merit:
- Increase in current causes increase in power due to P = VI.
- Increase in power causes increase in energy due to E = Pt.

For Excellence:
- Where I increases, V stays constant so P increases (P = VI).
- Where P increases, time stays constant so E increases (E = Pt).

questions.text: Describe and explain how the air in the room is heated by the convection heater, including how the air particles move in various parts of the room.
questions.expectedAnswer: Convection currents: hot air rises near heater (particles move faster, spread apart, lower density), cool air sinks (particles slower, closer together, higher density).
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- States warm air rises OR cold air sinks.
- States warm air is less dense OR cold air is more dense.

For Merit:
- Labelled description of particles getting further apart/less dense and rising.
- OR when it cools, particles closer together, more dense, and sink.

For Excellence:
- Full description of particles gaining kinetic energy from heater, moving faster and further apart (less dense, rising), then cooling at distance from heater, slowing down, moving closer together (more dense, sinking) — creating a convection current.

questions.text:
Mere's flatmate Hana measures the specific heat capacity (c) of water using a small immersion heater in a beaker.

She puts 0.400 kg of water in a beaker and heats it using a 20 V, 4.0 A immersion heater.

Define the term specific heat capacity.
questions.expectedAnswer: The energy required to heat one kilogram of a substance by one degree Celsius without changing state.

questions.text: Show that the electrical energy used by the immersion heater over 8 minutes (480 seconds) is 38 400 J.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- One correct equation and adds some numbers.

For Merit:
- Correct answer.
- Students may do this in one line: E = VIt = 20 × 4.0 × 480 = 38 400 J.

questions.text:
The table above shows Hana's experimental measurements of water temperature over time.

Calculate Hana's value for the specific heat capacity of water using her measurements. Show your working.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Selects correct equation.
- Has ΔT as 22 °C.

For Merit:
- Calculates a value for c with a minor error OR correct answer but incorrect unit.

For Excellence:
- Correct calculation (c ≈ 4360 J kg⁻¹ °C⁻¹) with correct unit.

questions.text:
Hana then compares her value with the textbook value of 4200 J kg⁻¹ °C⁻¹.

Discuss why her value and the textbook value are different.
questions.expectedAnswer: Hana's value will be different because not all electrical energy was transferred to the water.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Statement that mentions why the value is different, e.g.
- some energy heats the beaker or is lost to the surroundings.

For Merit:
- Statement AND link to heat transfer.
- Some energy is transferred to the glass beaker/lost to the atmosphere/not all transferred to the water.
- OR due to the thermometer reading being affected by position in the water.

questions.text:
Hana's value for the specific heat capacity of water is different from the textbook value.

Discuss how she could improve this experiment to get a more accurate result.

In your answer, you will need to:
- suggest ONE improvement to the experimental setup
- explain why this change would give a more accurate answer
- discuss the idea of heat transfer linked to this improvement.
questions.expectedAnswer: Suggested improvements include: insulate the beaker with a lid and foam wrapping, use a stirrer to ensure even heating, use a calorimeter instead of a beaker.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Describes a relevant improvement.
- Links improvement to a method of heat transfer.

For Merit:
- Describes a method to improve the accuracy AND explains how it helps with heat loss, linked to heat transfer (conduction, convection, or radiation).

For Excellence:
- Describes a method, explains how it reduces heat loss, AND links to heat transfer at a particle/wave level.
